title: Model-category localization detects weak equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category in the sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], with weak equivalences $W$, and let $\gamma:\mathcal M\to\mathcal H$ be an ordinary localization at $W$ (initial among functors sending $W$ to isomorphisms). Work in universes in which this localization exists. For every morphism $u:X\to Y$ of $\mathcal M$, $u\in W$ if and only if $\gamma(u)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal H$. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed cofibrant or fibrant.

source.place: Additional model-category foundation for the finite mapping-complex comparison: detecting weak equivalences after evaluation on cofibrant dg diagram values. This is not an assertion of a Stacks tag.

external.document: Mark Hovey, Model categories, https://ericmalm.net/ac/projects/symmetric-spectra/hovey--model-cats.pdf (read online; not archived in literature/)
external.place: Theorem 1.2.10(iv), with the forward implication furnished by the definition of localization.

proof.text: The forward implication is part of the localization hypothesis: $\gamma$ sends every member of $W$ to an isomorphism. We will use directly the model axioms stated in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. In a weak factorization system, either lifting class is closed under composition (solve two consecutive lifting problems), and left lifting classes are closed under coproducts with an identity (solve the problem on the nonidentity summand). Every isomorphism belongs to $W$: it lies in both lifting classes of $(C\cap W,F)$, since every square with an isomorphism on either side has a lift. In particular identities lie in $W$, so two-out-of-three gives closure of $W$ under composition. These elementary consequences justify the composite cofibrations and fibrations used below.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: forward implication and elementary lifting-class consequences of the definition

proof.text: Use the functorial factorizations in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] to obtain $q_Z:QZ\to Z$, a trivial fibration with $QZ$ cofibrant, and $r_Z:Z\to RZ$, a trivial cofibration with $RZ$ fibrant. For the given $u:X\to Y$, put $A=RQX$, $B=RQY$, and $f=RQ(u):A\to B$. These endpoints are fibrant by construction and cofibrant because $0\to QZ\to RQZ$ is a composite of cofibrations. Naturality gives $q_YQ(u)=u q_X$ and $f r_{QX}=r_{QY}Q(u)$. If $\gamma(u)$ is invertible, the first equality makes $\gamma(Q(u))$ invertible and the second makes $\gamma(f)$ invertible, since all four replacement arrows are in $W$. It remains to prove $f\in W$ for these bifibrant endpoints; no assumption on the original endpoints has been introduced.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: functorial replacement reduction, with both comparison squares written

proof.text: Factor $f$ as $A\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}B$, where $i$ is a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration, using [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. The object $E$ is cofibrant since $0\to A\to E$ is a composite of cofibrations, and fibrant since $E\to B\to *$ is a composite of fibrations. Since $\gamma(f)$ and $\gamma(i)$ are invertible, $\gamma(p)$ is invertible. Apply the representation clause of [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] to the cofibrant source $B$ and fibrant target $E$: choose $s:B\to E$ representing $\gamma(p)^{-1}$. Then $\gamma(ps)=1_{\gamma B}$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: represent the inverse of the fibration factor, not an inverse in the original category

proof.text: Apply the equality clause of [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] with source and target $B$, which is both cofibrant and fibrant. It gives a cylinder $B\xrightarrow{e_0,e_1}J\xrightarrow{c}B$ with $c\in W$, $ce_0=ce_1=1_B$, and $H:J\to B$ satisfying $He_0=ps$, $He_1=1_B$. Replace it by a good cylinder explicitly: factor $(e_0,e_1):B\amalg B\to J$ as a cofibration $k:B\amalg B\to K$ followed by a trivial fibration $v:K\to J$. Put $a_j=k\,\mathrm{in}_j$, $d=cv$, and $H_1=Hv$. Then $d\in W$, $da_j=1_B$, $H_1a_0=ps$ and $H_1a_1=1_B$. Since $B$ is cofibrant, $\mathrm{in}_0:B\to B\amalg B$ has the left lifting property against trivial fibrations: the map on the other summand lifts against $0\to B$. Thus $a_0$ is a cofibration. Two-out-of-three applied to $da_0=1_B$ makes $a_0$ also a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: extract the cylinder homotopy and improve its endpoints by one model factorization

proof.text: The square with top $s:B\to E$, left $a_0:B\to K$, right $p:E\to B$, and bottom $H_1:K\to B$ commutes by the equality $ps=H_1a_0$. The lifting axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] applies since $a_0$ is a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration. It yields $V:K\to E$ with $Va_0=s$ and $pV=H_1$. Set $t=Va_1:B\to E$. Then $pt=H_1a_1=1_B$. In particular $\gamma(t)=\gamma(p)^{-1}$, and therefore $\gamma(tp)=1_{\gamma E}$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: rectify the homotopy section to an actual section by one specified lifting square

proof.text: Apply the equality clause of [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] to $tp,1_E:E\to E$, with $E$ cofibrant and fibrant. Write the resulting cylinder as $E\xrightarrow{b_0,b_1}J_1\xrightarrow{c_1}E$ and its homotopy as $G:J_1\to E$, where $Gb_0=tp$, $Gb_1=1_E$, and $c_1b_j=1_E$ with $c_1\in W$. Two-out-of-three gives $b_0,b_1\in W$; from $Gb_1=1_E$ it then gives $G\in W$, and hence $tp=Gb_0\in W$. This uses only the displayed cylinder identities and two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], not a converse Whitehead theorem.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: a homotopy to the identity implies weak equivalence by the cylinder equations

proof.text: In the arrow category, $p:E\to B$ is a retract of $tp:E\to E$. The map from $p$ to $tp$ has source component $1_E$ and target component $t$, and the map back has source component $1_E$ and target component $p$. Their commutativity equations are $tp=tp$ and $ptp=p$; their composite on $p$ is $(1_E,pt)=(1_E,1_B)$. Retract closure of $W$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] now gives $p\in W$. Since $i\in W$, it follows that $f=pi\in W$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: the two arrow-category maps and their retract equation

proof.text: Return to the replacement squares of Step 2. The equality $f r_{QX}=r_{QY}Q(u)$ and $f,r_{QX},r_{QY}\in W$ imply $Q(u)\in W$ by two-out-of-three. The equality $u q_X=q_YQ(u)$ and $q_X,q_Y,Q(u)\in W$ then imply $u\in W$. Together with Step 1 this proves both directions for every morphism of $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, ordinary model-category detection foundation: transfer back along both replacement squares

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2: ordinary localization detection input, proved by functorial replacements, the Mathlib fundamental lemma, a cylinder lift, and an explicit retract. Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv) confirms the conclusion online but is not archived locally.
